title: Udyoga: the embassy, Krishna's counsel, Karna and Kunti
hook: Krishna speaks for peace before the whole Kuru court, Duryodhana walks out, and a plan to seize the envoy ends in a laugh
carry: no one could say it was never offered
tomorrow: Udyoga: the embassy, Krishna's counsel, Karna and Kunti

segments.voice: Yesterday Krishna carried Draupadi's words to Hastinapura, turned down a feast, and ate at Vidura's table. Your line was out of love, or out of need. Where did you eat, and with whom? Day eight hundred sixteen.

Morning in the great hall of the Kurus. Every seat is filled: Dhritarashtra on his throne, Bhishma, Drona, Vidura, Duryodhana and his brothers, Karna beside them. Krishna walks in, and the hall goes quiet. This is the moment the whole Udyoga has been building toward: a formal chance to stop the war, spoken face to face, in front of everyone who matters. Today, Krishna's counsel in the Kuru assembly, and what the court does with it.
screen: `THE HALL IS FULL.` → `KRISHNA WALKS IN.` → `A CHANCE TO STOP THE WAR.`

segments.voice: Krishna speaks to Dhritarashtra first, and his argument is simple. You can stop this, he says. Your sons and your nephews could stand together, and no one could stand against them. Peace would be your gain, not your loss. Give the Pandavas their share. Others speak after him. Old sages tell stories of pride brought low. Bhishma and Drona urge Duryodhana to make peace. Duryodhana hears them. And he refuses. He says, in effect, that he won't give the Pandavas even as much land as the point of a needle would cover, and he walks out of the hall. Then Gandhari, his mother, is sent for. He is called back to hear her, and she tells her son plainly that a person who can't rule his own anger and greed can't rule a kingdom. He leaves again. Outside, he and his friends make a plan: seize Krishna, tie him up, and the Pandavas will be helpless. Word reaches the hall. And Krishna laughs. The text says that as he laughed, his body blazed, and gods and heroes seemed to stream out of him, so bright the court had to shut their eyes. Only a few could look: Bhishma, Drona, Vidura and the sages, and Dhritarashtra, who was granted sight for that moment. Then the vision ends, and Krishna walks calmly out. The point of the scene isn't only the wonder. It's that Krishna came anyway. The night before, at Vidura's, he said he had come so that no one could blame him for not trying. So he made the whole case for peace in public, where no one could say it was never offered.
screen: `KRISHNA: PEACE IS YOUR GAIN` · `NOT EVEN A NEEDLE'S POINT OF LAND` · `GANDHARI: RULE YOUR OWN ANGER` · then, large: `A PLOT, A LAUGH, A BLAZING FORM`

segments.voice: Settle in and let your breathing slow. Krishna made his case for peace even though he expected a no. Bring to mind one good thing you've been holding back from saying because you think it won't be heard. Breathing in, let yourself say it silently, all the way through. Breathing out, let go of needing a yes. You've offered it, at least to yourself. If you pray, you can offer it in your prayer as well. The bell holds the time.
Udyoga. The getting ready, where Krishna makes the case for peace in front of the whole Kuru court, and Duryodhana refuses.

howItsDone: Krishna's embassy to the Kuru court is retold in Hindu storytelling and performance, and the form he reveals in the assembly is heard by some readers as a glimpse of the vision later shown to Arjuna.

match.prompt: the Kuru assembly — tap the pairs.
pairs: not a needle's point of land

myth: Bhishma and Drona urged Duryodhana to go to war
they urged him to make peace, as Krishna did.
Gandhari counseled her son in the assembly
she told him that someone who can't rule his anger and greed can't rule a kingdom.
they plotted to, but Krishna laughed, revealed a blazing form, and walked out.

fork.setup: you're Krishna. you've heard Duryodhana's friends plan to seize you in the hall. what do you do?
options: slip out quietly before they act.
laugh, and let the court see who you are.
call the Pandavas' army to Hastinapura.
fork.reveal: Krishna laughs, his body blazes with gods and heroes, and the court shuts its eyes. then he walks out calmly.

original.note: effort, getting ready; the embassy in the assembly is a public effort for peace.

trapdoor: what you thought: Krishna's embassy failed, so it was wasted.
what it means: he made the case for peace in public, so no one could say it was never offered.
what a scholar hears: the blazing form in the assembly anticipates the cosmic form Krishna shows Arjuna in the Bhagavad Gita.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Udyoga Parva (Bhagavat-yana), Krishna's speech in the Kuru assembly, the counsel of the sages, Bhishma, Drona and Gandhari, Duryodhana's refusal and plot, and Krishna's revealed form

notes: Audit: 'He knew Duryodhana's heart' (narrator mind-reading) replaced with Krishna's own stated reason to Vidura the night before (Ganguli, Bhagavat-yana: he tries for peace so none can blame him); confirm wording.

All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: Krishna's speech to Dhritarashtra; the sages' stories (e.g., Parasurama, Kanva, Narada); Bhishma's and Drona's counsel; Gandhari called to the hall and her counsel on mastering the senses and anger.
Duryodhana's 'not even as much land as the point of a needle' is widely known; confirm its placement in Ganguli's Udyoga text and wording before finalizing.

Confirm the plot to seize Krishna (Duryodhana, Karna, Shakuni, Duhshasana), Krishna's laugh and revealed form, and that Bhishma, Drona, Vidura (and sages) could look, with Dhritarashtra granted temporary sight.
The trapdoor links this form to the Bhagavad Gita's vision; a Keeper may prefer different wording.
